sections.title: Market Pulse: Indices Close Down Amid Economic Data, Weekly Gains for Tech

items.headline: U.S. Markets Decline on Friday; Tech Leads Weekly Rebound
items.summary: U.S. equity markets closed lower on Friday, August 1, 2026, with all major indices seeing significant drops for the day. This daily downturn came despite a strong weekly performance for tech stocks, which led a broader market rebound throughout the week. The market grappled with news of sluggish Q2 economic growth and persistent inflation concerns, while rising mortgage rates added pressure. Not financial advice.

items.headline: Amazon.com Surges on Strong Performance
items.summary: E-commerce giant Amazon.com Inc. saw significant gains, reflecting continued strong market positioning.

items.headline: Dexcom Inc. Climbs
items.summary: Dexcom Inc. posted a notable increase in its stock price.

items.headline: Monolithic Power Systems Gains
items.summary: Monolithic Power Systems Inc. experienced a strong upward movement.

items.headline: Alphabet Rises on Blowout Earnings
items.summary: Alphabet Inc. (Class C) shares jumped after the company reported blowout earnings, largely driven by AI-powered growth in Google Cloud and a resurgence in its search business.

items.headline: Microsoft Leads Weekly Tech Surge
items.summary: Microsoft saw a substantial weekly gain, closing up 22% for the week, propelled by strong earnings across all segments and robust Azure revenue growth, including AI workloads.

items.headline: Specific Top Losers Data Unavailable for August 1, 2026
items.summary: Detailed information on specific top individual stock losers with price and percentage changes for Friday, August 1, 2026, was not readily available at the time of this report.

items.headline: U.S. Economy Grew at Sluggish 1.5% in Q2
items.summary: The U.S. economy expanded at a modest 1.5% annual pace from April through June 2026, a deceleration from the 2.1% growth in the first three months of the year. Consumer spending, however, showed an increase, and business investment, particularly in artificial intelligence, remained strong.

items.headline: Federal Reserve Holds Rates Steady Amid Dissent and Persistent Inflation
items.summary: The Federal Reserve maintained its key interest rate unchanged this week, although three officials expressed dissent in favor of higher rates. This decision comes as the central bank continues to grapple with persistently high inflation, which, despite slowing, remains above the Fed's 2% target.

items.headline: 30-Year Mortgage Rates Hit One-Year High
items.summary: The average 30-year U.S. mortgage rate climbed for the fourth consecutive week, reaching 6.66% from 6.58% previously. This marks the highest level in a year, posing a setback for prospective homebuyers.

items.headline: Consumer Discretionary Leads Friday Gains; Materials Lag
items.summary: On Friday, Consumer Discretionary (+3.23%), Energy (+1.02%), and Industrials (+0.81%) were among the leading sectors. Conversely, Materials (-2.38%), Utilities (-0.73%), and Health Care (-0.57%) were among the lagging sectors.

items.headline: Tech Sector Leads Weekly Rebound, Driven by 'Magnificent Seven'
items.summary: Last week saw a strong tech-driven rebound, with the Nasdaq index leading overall market performance, significantly influenced by the 'Magnificent Seven' stocks. This indicates a potential broadening of market leadership beyond solely large-cap tech.

items.headline: Key Earnings Reports: Alphabet Shines, Meta Falls, Microsoft Strong
items.summary: Earnings season continues to unfold, with Alphabet ($GOOG, $GOOGL) delivering a 'blowout' report driven by AI growth. Meta Platforms ($META), however, sold off due to weaker-than-expected numbers and guidance. Microsoft ($MSFT) reported strong results across all fronts, with significant growth in its Azure cloud services.

items.headline: Upcoming Earnings Reports This Week
items.summary: Clorox and Marriott International are scheduled to report earnings on Monday. SpaceX and McDonald's will release their results on Tuesday, followed by Expedia Group on Wednesday.

items.headline: Bitcoin Falls Below $63,000
items.summary: Bitcoin experienced a notable decline on Friday, falling below the $63,000 mark and reaching its lowest level in approximately two weeks.

items.headline: U.S.-Mexico-Canada Trade Limbo Concerns Businesses
items.summary: Texas businesses are expressing concern over the financial implications of the ongoing uncertainty surrounding the renegotiation of the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA). New tariffs on Mexican and Canadian imports are creating significant pressure.
